steps.label: 8 foot ladder
steps.quote: In this example, we have an 8 foot ladder that we are going to lean against a wall.

steps.label: base is 2 feet from the wall
steps.quote: If we incline the ladder so that its base is 2 feet from the wall, the ladder forms an angle of nearly 75.5 degrees degrees with the ground.

steps.label: distance from the wall
steps.quote: The ratio of the distance from the wall (a – adjacent), to the length of the ladder (h – hypotenuse), is 2/8 = .25.

steps.label: opposite to the hypotenuse
steps.quote: The ratio of the opposite to the hypotenuse is .967 and defined to be the sine of the angle c = 75.5 degrees.

steps.label: base is 4 feet from the wall
steps.quote: Now suppose we incline the 8 foot ladder so that its base is 4 feet from the wall.

steps.label: ratio of the adjacent to the hypotenuse
steps.quote: The angle is 60 degrees, and the ratio of the adjacent to the hypotenuse is now 4/8 = .5 .
